# 4 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Love Overcome by Piety

---

**1** O reason of the children, tyrant over passions! O piety, dearer to the mother than her own children!

**2** The mother had two choices before her: piety and the temporary safety of her seven sons.

**3** She chose to love religion more; she chose to love the immortality of virtue more.

**4** How can I put into words the yearning of parents for their children? We imprint upon the soul of a little child a wondrous likeness of ourselves in both mind and form and this is especially true of mothers, who feel the deepest bond of sympathy with their children.

**5** The more tender the feeling and the more heartfelt the love, the harder it is for a mother to let go of her children.

**6** And yet the mother of the seven sons was not overcome; she endured it all.

**7** Her reason was stronger than her feelings; her devotion to God was stronger than her love for her children.

**8** How was she not persuaded by her natural feelings? How was she not softened by her tender love? How did she not weep as her children died before her eyes?

**9** She had planted reason deep in her heart, and that became her stronghold.

**10** She had raised her sons in the law and in the love of virtue, and that upbringing was bearing its fruit.

**11** She had set her reason above her passion, and when the moment of ultimate testing arrived, reason held firm.

**12** How shall I describe what it means for parents to love their children? We imprint upon the soul of a little child a wondrous likeness of ourselves in mind and form.

**13** Mothers feel this most of all; they carry a tenderness for their children that goes deeper than any other bond.

**14** The more tender the love, the more devastating is the loss of a child.

**15** Yet the mother of the seven was not overcome; she endured it for the sake of her devotion to God.

**16** O woman greater than Ananias, Azariah, and Mishael! O woman more admirable than the great patriarch Abraham!

**17** Abraham did not hesitate to sacrifice his son Isaac on the altar and this woman did not hesitate to give up seven sons to the law.

**18** By her reason she proved herself more admirable than Abraham; by her love for God she proved herself more enduring than the three young men in the furnace.

**19** O most admirable mother! O most blessed woman! O devotion to piety beyond all human praise!

**20** Through her piety and her reason she mastered all her passions.

**21** I urge you, people of God, to follow the example of this woman and the seven sons and through reason governed by devotion to God to conquer your passions.

**22** For devotion to God is truly the mother of all virtues and the governor of all passions.

**23** Through it the seven brothers and their mother overcame tyranny, torture, and death itself.
